newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CURVE STEEPENS IN BELGIAN BONDS, PLAYERS UNCERTAIN.
newsitem.headline: CURVE STEEPENS IN BELGIAN BONDS, PLAYERS UNCERTAIN.

text.p: The corrective steepening in the yield curve of Belgian linear bonds continued on Thursday, with buying seen of five-year OLOs and selling in 10-year paper, but traders said the future was uncertain and players were cautious.

"The curve steepened five basis points yesterday and another three today," one trader said. "But I am not so bullish and if we rise another four to five basis points I see it as an opportunity to put on flatteners."
"The market is not decided where it wants to go. Dollar/mark is a dominant influence and people are really reassessing their positions," he added.
The market is also nervous about possible German interest rate moves, although the mark strengthened slightly on Thursday despite a lack of rate action by the Bundesbank.
A rumour, quickly officially denied, that German Chancellor Helmut Kohl was dead or sick barely dented the bond markets.
"The Bund future briefly dipped 10 basis points, but that was all and it quickly recovered," one trader said.
The markets also took initial U.S. August jobless claims -- which were in line with expectations -- calmly in their stride.
Traders said that technically markets looked reasonably solid. "I am looking for 102.25/35 on the Bund and would not be surprised to see Treasuries at 115.05," one trader said.
The Bund future was at 101.98 in late trading on Thursday and Treasuries were at 114.25.
They expected money market rates, which eased again on Thursday, to move higher in the short to medium term.
One-week repos yielded 3.38/43 percent late on Thursday, dwon from 3.49/54 on Wednesday.
